title: Limits of the level-independent fall: level superpositions, records, the operator under the factor

key_results.statement: Exact in the gradients and in $\kappa$, for every $\alpha$, smooth $g$, $\chi$, $\lambda$ and chain: $p_x=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2p^{(k)}_x$ and $\bar x_{\rm lab}=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2\bar x_k$; it rests on the conservation of the level and the orthonormality of the $\lvert f_k\rangle$.

Class: every $\alpha$, every smooth $g$ concentrated at $p_0$; limits in this order: first order in the gradients, long chain, $\Lambda\to\infty$ at fixed $g$, then $\delta p\to0$ (mean and variance only), leading order in $\kappa$. Drift acceleration $\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$, with an exact bound for every $\Lambda>0$ that is not uniform in $\delta p$; it is the same for all $\alpha$ iff $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$ is level-independent (at rest: line 1 or 2 of (4.19), no new condition).

Class: starts at rest, fixed smooth $g$; first order, long chain. $D=\tfrac14\lambda^4\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(\langle a_{\cdot,\sigma}\rangle_g)+E$ with the bound $\lvert E\rvert\le r\lambda^3\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\alpha}+r^2\lambda^2$ ($r$ depends on $g$); the sharp-label limit is taken on the coefficient of $\lambda^4$ only and gives $\tfrac14\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(a_{\cdot,\sigma}(0))$.

Class $\mathcal C$, $\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2=1/N$, sharp-label limit of the $\lambda^4$ coefficient of $D$: zero for the variants (a), (c); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2m^2\mathcal V_N$ for (b1), (b2); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2c_{\rm f}^2\mathcal V_N$ for (f).

Zero gradients, sharp-label limit (every sequence concentrated at $p_0$ with $\delta p\to0$): $v_k\to\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)$; for $\sin2p_0\neq0$ the sharp-label velocities of two levels are equal iff $\tau_k^4/(M_k^2+\tau_k^2\sin^2p_0)=\tau_{k'}^4/(M_{k'}^2+\tau_{k'}^2\sin^2p_0)$; in $\mathcal C$ they are strictly ordered.

Bound, every start concentrated at $p_0$: $\lvert v_k-\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)\rvert\le\tfrac12\sup\lvert\omega_k'''\rvert\delta p^2$, so $v_k\neq v_{k'}$ for $\delta p<\delta p_*$; exact for every smooth $g$: $v_k=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g$, and a start of finite width can have equal velocities in all levels (example $\lvert g\rvert^2=1+\epsilon\cos(p-p_0)$, all $v_k=0$).

Exact in the gradients, any normalized level component: $\mathrm d\bar p_k/\mathrm d\lambda=-\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}c^\dagger B_kc+(c^\dagger B_kc)(p_0+\pi)$, the last term being the weight that crosses the cut of the arc.

First order at fixed $\lambda$ and start, long chain, every smooth $g$: rate of the mean label $\langle\pi_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g-\lvert g(p_0+\pi)\rvert^2\pi_{k,\sigma}(p_0+\pi)$; for sequences of starts at rest with $\delta p\to0$ and $\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2\to0$ it tends to $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$.

Bound, every start at rest: the first-order rate differs from $(1-\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2)(\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k)$ by at most $\tfrac12\sup\lvert\pi_{k,\sigma}''\rvert\delta p^2$; for sequences with $\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2\to c_{\rm cut}\neq1$ the limiting rate is level-independent iff $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$ is, and together with a level-independent drift acceleration $a\neq0$ iff also $\tau_k^2/M_k$ is (impossible in $\mathcal C$); for $c_{\rm cut}=1$ it is zero in every level.

Exact with the medium in the level components: $P(a;\lambda)=\frac1N\sum_{k,k'}\alpha_{k'}^{*}\alpha_k\Gamma_{kk'}(\lambda)e^{2\pi i(k-k')a/N}$; at leading order in $\kappa$ the $\Gamma_{kk'}$ of the effective body contract.

Exact, every smooth $g$: $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}=e^{-i(V_k-V_{k'})\lambda}\langle\cos\tfrac{\theta_k-\theta_{k'}}2e^{-i\sigma(\omega_k-\omega_{k'})\lambda}\rangle_g$; for even $g$, $\Gamma_{kk'}$ is exactly even in the gradients.

Exact, every smooth $g$, $p_0$, $\lambda$: $\Gamma_{kk'}[g;\text{gradients}]=\Gamma_{kk'}[g^-;-\text{gradients}]$; $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ has no first-order term for starts of definite parity $g(-p)=\pm g(p)$ and for pairs with equal $(\tau,M)$; a nonzero second-order term is not shown by this.

Exact, every smooth complex $g$, every $p_0$ and $\lambda\ge0$, first order at fixed $\lambda$ and start, leading order in $\kappa$: the first-order term $\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}$ (in-branch integral plus $\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}$); where $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\neq0$, $(\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert)_1=\operatorname{Re}(\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}/\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'})$; at a zero of $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}$, $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert=\lvert\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}\rvert$ to first order.

Exact, every smooth $g$: the first-order inter-branch amplitude $a_{k,\perp}$, with $b_{\perp,k}=\frac{\tau_k\sin p}{\omega_k}(G_k-M_kg_{\zeta,k})$; bound $\lVert a_{k,\perp}\rVert\le A_{k,\perp}(\lambda)$, linear in $\lambda$ with the coefficient $\frac{\tau_k^3\mathsf b_k}{2M_k^3}\langle\sin^4p\rangle_g^{1/2}$; it is not bounded in $\lambda$.

Exact, every smooth $g$: the inter-branch part $\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}$ of the first-order term, with the bound $\lvert\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}\rvert\le\tfrac12(\tfrac{\tau_k}{M_k}+\tfrac{\tau_{k'}}{M_{k'}})\langle\sin^2p\rangle_g^{1/2}(A_{k,\perp}+A_{k',\perp})$.

Bound, every start at rest: $1-\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}(\lambda)\rvert\le[\tfrac12\lambda\sup\lvert\omega_k''-\omega_{k'}''\rvert+\tfrac18(\tfrac{\tau_k}{M_k}+\tfrac{\tau_{k'}}{M_{k'}})^2]\delta p^2$, a sufficient condition for $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\neq0$.

Order estimate; class: real Gaussian starts at rest (E1); range (E3) and (7.32); second order in the gradients, leading order in $\kappa$: $1-\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert\simeq\tfrac12\delta x^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})^2\lambda^2+\tfrac{\lambda^4}{32\delta x^2}(\tfrac{\tau_{k'}^2}{M_{k'}}\pi_k-\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}\pi_{k'})^2$, $\pi_k=\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$; with a level-independent fall $a$ it vanishes iff $a=0$ or $\tau_k^2/M_k=\tau_{k'}^2/M_{k'}$.

Order estimate of the inter-branch part neglected in (7.10): $N_\perp\sim\frac{\tau^2\mathsf b^2}{M^4}(1+M\lambda)(1+\nu\lambda\delta p^2)^2$; it rests on the exact bound (7.29) and on second-order inter-branch terms that are estimated, not derived.

Order estimate; class (F1): narrow starts at rest with smooth complex $g$; range (F2), (F3); first order at fixed $\lambda$ and start, then leading order in $\delta p$: $(\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert)_1\simeq\Delta\nu_{kk'}[\tfrac14\lambda^3\varpi_{kk'}\langle p^3\rangle_g-\tfrac\sigma2\lambda^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})J_g]$.

Exact at first order jointly in $G_k$, $\mathcal F_k$, $g_{\zeta,k}$ and $\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$, every smooth $g$ and every $\chi$: the first-order velocity of a branch start does not change when $X$ is not sharp; (4.7), (4.16), (4.19) are unchanged.

Exact, pointwise in $p$, zero gradients: the second-order coefficient $v_2(p,\lambda)$ of the velocity in $\varepsilon=\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$, with the secular term $\tfrac\sigma2\lambda^2\omega'''$ and the oscillating term $-\tfrac\sigma2\lambda^2\theta'^2\omega'\cos2\omega\lambda$ of the same order in $\lambda$.

Zero gradients, every fixed smooth $g$, expansion in $\kappa$ at fixed $\lambda$: $v=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+\kappa^2\sigma_X^2[\tfrac12\lambda^2\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g+R_2]+\kappa^3\mu_3[-\tfrac16\lambda^3\sigma\langle\omega_k''''\rangle_g+R_3]+O(\kappa^4)$; bound on $R_2$ exact, linear in $\lambda$, not uniform for $\delta p\to0$; $R_3=O(\lambda^{5/2})$ is an order estimate at fixed $g$.

Bound, every smooth $g$, $\lambda_1\ge0$, $\Lambda>0$: the second-order coefficient of the window-averaged acceleration obeys $\lvert\overline{a_2}-\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g\bar\lambda\rvert\le(2c_1[g]\bar\lambda+2c_0)/\Lambda$; the sharp-label limit can be combined with the long window only if $X_g/\Lambda\to0$; at a fixed window and a sharp label an oscillating term of the order of the secular one remains.

Secular acceleration (derivative of the secular velocity term; limits: expansion in $\kappa$, secular coefficient at fixed smooth $g$, then sharp-label limit of the coefficient; exact coefficient): $\delta a^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}=-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda v(4+3\omega_k''/\omega_k)$, zero at rest, first order in $v$; level-independent at leading order in $v$ iff $\tau_k/M_k$ is; not in $\mathcal C$.

Secular acceleration at third order (same limits; coefficient of the adiabatic term exact, its dominance rests on the order estimate of $R_3$): $\delta a^{(3)}_{k,\sigma}=-\tfrac12\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\sigma\omega_k''''(p_0)$, at rest $\tfrac\sigma2\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(4+\tfrac{3\tau_k^2}{M_k^2})$; odd in the branch, only for a skewed $X$; not level-independent in $\mathcal C$.

The secular record terms in the background of (17.15) of 03-ilang-space/17-motion, with $d_0=\kappa\sigma_X$, $v_{\max,k}=\tau_kd_0$, $u=d_0v$: $[-\lambda(4d_0^2+\tfrac{3v_{\max,k}^2}{M_k^2})u+\tfrac{\sigma\gamma_X}2\lambda^2\tfrac{v_{\max,k}^2}{M_k}(4d_0^2+\tfrac{3v_{\max,k}^2}{M_k^2})]\hat e$.

The secular record terms (only these) are smaller than the drift acceleration (4.7) at rest where $\varrho_2<1$ and $\varrho_3<1$; weak records has to mean at least $\varrho_2,\varrho_3,\varrho_{2,\rm rest}\le\delta_{\rm acc}$ for every level on the observed range of windows and $v$; sufficiency is not shown.

Bound-based condition for the rest of the window-averaged acceleration at second order in $\kappa$: $\varrho_{2,\rm rest}=\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\frac{2c_1[g]\bar\lambda+2c_0}{\Lambda}\frac{M_k}{\tau_k^2\lvert\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k\rvert}$; not uniform for $\delta p\to0$; the third-order rest has only an order estimate.

On-site block $(1+gx)[M_k\sigma_3+u_k]-\mathcal F_Ux$, branch starts at rest, drift acceleration in the limits of (4.11): $a_{k,\pm}(0)=-g\tau_k^2\pm\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)$ (exact in these limits).

Fall from rest the same for all levels: upper branch iff $\tau_k^2[\tfrac{\mathcal F_U-gu_k}{M_k}-g]$ is level-independent; lower branch iff $\tau_k^2[-\tfrac{\mathcal F_U-gu_k}{M_k}-g]$ is; both with one value $a$ iff $gu_k=\mathcal F_U$ and $g\tau_k^2=-a$ for all $k$.

Exact: $C_{\rm eff}\mapsto C_{\rm eff}+c\mathbb 1$ acts as $(u_k,\mathcal F_U)\mapsto(u_k+c,\mathcal F_U+gc)$; well defined are $g$, $M_k$, $u_k-u_{k'}$, $\mathcal F_U-gu_k$; not well defined are $u_k$, '$u_k=0$ for all $k$' and '$u_k\propto M_k$'.

Table of the orders (gradients, $v$, $M_k/\tau_k$, $\kappa$, $\lambda$) at which the lattice, the drift velocity, a superposition of levels, the records, the operator under the factor and a plain gradient change the level-independent fall and the relation (4.24), with the class of starts and the status of each entry.

open_issues: Item 1(f), open part: the second-order term of |Γ| for every start other than the real Gaussian starts (E1), including whether it is nonzero for a given start of definite parity; the leading form of the first-order term for starts at rest that are not narrow or outside (F2); the cases in which (7.25) vanishes.

(7.10) is an order estimate under (E1)–(E3); its inter-branch estimate (7.32) rests on the exact first-order bound (7.29), but the second-order inter-branch amplitude and the mixed terms are estimated, not derived; no bound.
(7.25) and (7.26) are order estimates under (F1)–(F3): the inter-branch remainder is bounded by (7.30), the remainder of the expansion in δp is estimated, not bounded.

Item 1(e): for starts of finite width the level-independence of the rate (7.7) is not reduced to a condition on the level data; for sequences with limiting cut weight 1 the limiting rate of the arc mean vanishes in every level.
(7.3): the constant r of the bound on E depends on g; no bound uniform in δp is derived, so nothing is stated on D at fixed λ in the sharp-label limit.

R_3 = O(λ^(5/2)) in (7.14) is an order estimate without a constant, and (7.16) as the fastest-growing third-order part rests on it; the acceleration of a sharp label at a fixed window is not characterized; sufficiency of the weak-record conditions of Step 8, part 3 is not shown.
The estimate of ϱ_2 for a fall from rest mixes κ² with a gradient (third order, out of scope) and is not derived.
(7.17) uses v_max,k = τ_k d_0 for level-dependent τ_k; the quoted bound (5.11) of 04-ilang-time/05-moving-clock is stated for one τ.
The effect of an operator under the factor on the relation (4.24) outside the class C needs the clock rate of that body, which is not among the quoted inputs.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (7.15), (7.16), (7.10), ϱ_2, ϱ_3 and (7.3) with costs in units of 1/λ and dimensionless labels

One level (α_k = δ_kk0), a sharp X, and a plain gradient only: reductions of (7.1), (7.2), (7.3), (7.8), (7.11), (7.14)–(7.17); rigid shift of the label weight reproduces (7.28) with the cut weight; (7.29) reproduces the first-order term of Step 7
Short-λ expansion of (7.13) against the double commutator, and agreement of (7.7) with (4.16) for a plain gradient
